newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaireans hail rebel leader as source of new life.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans hail rebel leader as source of new life.

text.p: Zaireans in two towns taken by rebels in the country's copperbelt are hailing the forces of Laurent Kabila as the source of a new life free of harassment from government soldiers.

People happily bathed and did their laundry in the Luapula River on Friday on the outskirts of Kasenga, a town 220 km (130 miles) northeast of Lubumbashi, the country's copper capital and second biggest city which fell to the rebels last weekend.

As the rebels move around the town, men and women throw flour at them as a symbol of gratitude and shout "Kabila is power, Kabila is water", equating the leader with the life- giving liquid they consider to be sacred.
Up to 300 local men daily are reported to be joining Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire.

"We took Kasenga in the early hours of Saturday morning. Twenty-two rebels walked into the town and we met no resistance. We were welcomed by the local people," General Nawez-Jean Yav told Reuters in an interview.
He said his troops also took Minga, halfway between Lubumbashi and Kasenga, in a battle in which 17 Zairean soldiers were killed.
Yav added that his men had captured 14 mercenaries, including Burundians, former Rwandan government soldiers and troops from Angola's former rebel UNITA movement.
Pianga Ngombe, a member of the Zairean civil guard in Kasenga, told Reuters he was considering joining the rebel forces who had disarmed him.
"I have heard that the rebels had liberated many parts of eastern Zaire and had not harmed the people. We knew we were going to be liberated, so I decided to stay," he said.
Hotel owner Ernest Devildi said government soldiers had harassed the locals, refused to pay their bills at the hotel and and had looted shops before fleeing the rebel advance.

Kabila's forces, which have seized control of a quarter of the country in just six months, were reported to have marched into the diamond mining capital of Mbuji-Mayi earlier on Friday and be encircling Lubumbashi which they say is their next target.
The opposing sides in Zaire's civil war, which threatens to tear apart the huge central African country, were scheduled to meet face-to-face for the first time on Saturday.
